eyebrow: SparkSession — where every PySpark script starts
caption: Every read, every DataFrame, every query goes through this one spark object.

eyebrow: Reading the real NYC Taxi dataset
code:
trips = spark.read.parquet("/data/nyc_taxi/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet")
trips.printSchema()
trips.show(5)

# root
#  |-- VendorID: integer (nullable = true)
#  |-- tpep_pickup_datetime: timestamp (nullable = true)
#  |-- passenger_count: double (nullable = true)
#  |-- trip_distance: double (nullable = true)
#  |-- fare_amount: double (nullable = true)
caption: printSchema() is PySpark's version of pandas' df.dtypes — check column names and types first.

eyebrow: Transformations vs. actions — Spark delays work
code:
filtered = trips.filter(trips.fare_amount > 0)   # nothing runs yet
grouped = filtered.groupBy("VendorID")             # still nothing runs

grouped.count().show()                             # THIS triggers the work
caption: filter() and groupBy() are transformations — just recorded steps. show()/count()/collect() are actions that actually execute them.
